output.explanation:
Noted for all future write-ups (saved to memory). Now the Z-Defence deviations from the ground up, then a proposed todo.

## First, the concepts you need

**The z-score here is a one-proportion z-test.** Take a word 𝑤 and a label 𝑦. Among the 𝑛 training rows that contain 𝑤, some fraction 𝑝̂ carry label 𝑦. If 𝑤 carried no information about the label, that fraction would be a coin-flip with bias 𝑝₀ = the label's overall rate in the training set. For 𝑛 coin flips with bias 𝑝₀, the observed fraction has standard deviation √(𝑝₀(1−𝑝₀)/𝑛). So

$$z = \frac{\hat p - p_0}{\sqrt{p_0(1-p_0)/n}}$$

is "how many standard deviations above chance is this word's association with this label." Under no association 𝑧 is roughly standard-normal (mean 0, SD 1). A trigger word inserted into 𝑛 target-label rows and nowhere else has 𝑝̂ = 1, so 𝑧 ≈ √𝑛 · √((1−𝑝₀)/𝑝₀) — for 𝑛 = 600 that is on the order of 20–40. Nothing benign gets near that. That's why the method needs no model.

**Document frequency vs term frequency.** Document frequency counts a word once per row it appears in; term frequency counts every occurrence. The z-test above is only a valid proportion test under document frequency (each row is one trial). Z-Defence's Eq. 2 uses an indicator 𝟙(𝑎 ∈ 𝒙ᵢ), i.e. document frequency. Its repo, however, counts term frequency. CMT uses document frequency — faithful to the paper's equation, not the repo.

**"Label-conditioned feature."** Z-Defence never flags a *word*; it flags a *(word, label) pair*. "Word 𝑤 with label 𝑦 has extreme 𝑧" is the object on the shortlist. A row is removed only if it contains 𝑤 **and** carries label 𝑦. That "and" is the deviation that matters most below.

**FRR / FAR.** The paper's detection metrics: false rejection rate = fraction of clean rows removed; false acceptance rate = fraction of poisoned rows kept. CMT instead grades a continuous per-row score by AUROC — the probability a random poisoned row outscores a random clean one. Any thresholded rule (flag if score > τ) is one point on the AUROC curve, so a continuous score whose ordering respects the paper's rule is a *monotone relaxation* of it — the AUROC summarizes all thresholds at once. That relaxation is fine *if* the ordering matches; it is not fine if the port scores different rows high than the paper would.

**Node addresses and hashed params (CMT-specific).** Every scan node lives at `scan_train+<recipe>+<hash of params>`. Changing a default that is *not* a param silently changes what an existing address means; adding a new hashed param with a paper-faithful default mints new addresses and leaves old ones reachable under an explicit spelling. The tree's rule (D22, and the `clibe` `perturb_site` precedent) is: never fix a kernel in place — add the param.

## The deviations, paper-vs-port

I've numbered them so the todo can cite them. "Paper" = He et al., EMNLP 2023 text; "repo" = the pinned `z_filtering.py`.

**Z1 — Row-label conditioning dropped (mechanism; the one to fix).**
Paper: shortlist (𝑤,𝑦) pairs; remove row 𝑖 iff ∃(𝑤,𝑦) on the shortlist with 𝑤 ∈ 𝒙ᵢ *and* 𝑦ᵢ = 𝑦 (§3 "discard all training instances containing these label-conditioned features"; repo lines 88–93 do exactly this).
CMT: suspicion(row 𝑖) = max over its tokens of max over *all* labels of 𝑧(𝑡,𝑦) — the row's own label 𝑦ᵢ is never consulted (`paper.py:104-116`, `tokenize.py:118-122`).
Why it matters for you specifically: under a boolean trigger, a *present-but-non-activating* row contains trigger words but is correctly labeled clean. Paper: (trigger, clean) has strongly *negative* 𝑧, so that row is not touched. CMT: the row inherits the trigger's huge 𝑧 for the *target* label and scores as high as a poisoned row. This is a direct candidate explanation for the port's partial-contrast collapse (0.994 activation → 0.656 partial); it would need a read-side re-derivation to confirm, but the mechanism is unambiguous. It also means the current a123 series is a label-agnostic variant, not Z-Defence.
Suggest: **fix**, as a new hashed param `row_label_conditioning: "own_label" | "max_over_labels"`, default `own_label` (paper); old series stays reachable and gets relabeled "CMT label-agnostic variant" in every report.

**Z2 — Sidedness (mechanism; small).**
Paper: "high magnitude" / "|𝑝̂ − 𝑝| large" — two-sided; repo `mean ± 20·std`.
CMT: only positive 𝑧, floored at 0.
On two labels the two are identical (a negative 𝑧 for one label is the same-magnitude positive 𝑧 for the other). On multi-class cls they are not, and once Z1 is fixed they diverge more: under own-label conditioning a row containing a word that is *anti*-correlated with its own label would be flagged by the paper and not by CMT.
Suggest: **fix alongside Z1** as `two_sided: true` (default paper), or disclose if you'd rather keep magnitude out of it. Cheap either way.

**Z3 — Threshold + removal + retrain → continuous ranking (scope; disclose).**
Paper: shortlist at ~18 SD outliers of the z distribution (repo 20), remove rows, retrain, report FRR/FAR and ASR/CACC.
CMT: no threshold, no removal, no retrain; continuous max-z per row, AUROC. This is a kind-level ruling already made tree-wide (the sanitize stage was deleted; every train_scan is detection-terminal), and the ranking is the monotone relaxation of the paper's OR-over-tokens rule.
Suggest: **disclose**, and optionally emit the paper's binary flag at the outlier threshold as a *companion field* (recorded as data, never the graded score) so FRR/FAR can be printed beside the AUROC. Note the paper/repo disagree (18 vs 20 SD) — pick 18 and record the repo's 20 on the row.

**Z4 — Feature set: unigrams only (scope; disclose).**
Paper: Z-Token = unigrams *and bigrams*; Z-Tree = constituency ancestor paths via Stanza; default reported config Z-Seq = tree then token.
CMT: unigrams only.
Bigrams: the paper's own appendix finds them roughly comparable and its repo has the bigram z commented out; CMT's triggers are inserted at random positions so adjacent-pair features rarely see two trigger words together. Z-Tree: aimed at *syntactic-template* triggers, which CMT does not run, and needs a Stanza parser dependency.
Suggest: **disclose both** with that reasoning; bigrams as an optional `ngram: 1|2` param only if you want to test conjunctive triggers via adjacency (I'd skip it).

**Z5 — Null prior 𝑝₀ (no deviation from paper; disclose the repo mismatch).**
Paper: 𝑝(𝑦∣𝑎) ≈ 𝑝(𝑦) "derived from the training set" — the empirical label rate. CMT: 𝑝ᵧ = 𝑛ᵧ/𝑁 — the same. Repo: uniform 1/|labels| on the live line, empirical on a commented-out line. On imbalanced or binarized generative settings these differ.
Suggest: **disclose** "faithful to the paper's stated null; the repo's live line uses uniform."

**Z6 — Tokenizer (paper-silent; disclose).**
Paper does not say. Repo: whitespace split, no lowercasing. CMT: `\w+` on lowercased text (punctuation stripped, contractions fragmented, "Actually"/"actually" merged).
Suggest: **disclose** as a CMT choice; note case-folding could merge a capitalized inserted trigger with its lowercase natural occurrences, which *dilutes* 𝑝̂ for that word — direction is toward a weaker detector, worth stating.

**Z7 — Counting unit (faithful to paper, not repo).** Document frequency (Eq. 2 indicator) — CMT matches; repo uses term frequency. Disclose the repo mismatch only.

**Z8 — Label 𝑦 on generative settings (CMT extension; disclose).**
Paper: classification labels. CMT: on jailbreak/refusal, the response is binarized comply/refuse by the refusal-keyword predicate (`label_mode.py`), because raw free-text outputs make every label count ≈ 1. Beyond the paper's scope; the binarization is a CMT design decision and should be on the manifest as such.

**Z9 — Stop-words (faithful).** Neither paper nor CMT filters. Already adjudicated in ledger `scan-stopword-fidelity` as "none". Record as implemented/faithful.

[... trimmed at 60 lines ...]
